([[Lakeville, Minnesota]]) * [[Hopkins High School|Hopkins]]
([[Minnetonka, Minnesota]]) | college = [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] (2019–2020) | draft_year = 2020 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 22 | draft_team = [[Denver Nuggets]] | career_start = 2020 | years1 = {{nbay|2020|start}}–present | team1 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | highlights = * [[NBA champion]] ([[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]) * First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] ([[2019–20 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2020]]) * [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 Freshman of the Year]] (2020) * [[Pac-12]] All-Freshman team (2020) }} '''Ezekiel Tobechukwu''' "'''Zeke'''" '''Nnaji''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|n|ɑː|dʒ|i}} {{respell|NAH|jee}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 17, 2024}} born January 9, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Denver Nuggets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] and was drafted 22nd overall by the Nuggets in the [[2020 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Nnaji was born in [[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]]. He played [[baseball]] and [[soccer]] before starting [[basketball]] due to his height. He has played the piano since first grade. Nnaji composes his own music.{{cite web |last=Max |first=Mike |title=Top High School Basketball Player Doubles As Concert Pianist |url=https://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2018/12/28/high-school-basketball-player-concert-pianist-zeke-nnaji/ |website=[[WCCO-TV]] |access-date=November 27, 2019 |date=December 28, 2018}} ==High school career== Nnaji started playing high school basketball for [[Lakeville North High School]] in [[Lakeville, Minnesota]], before transferring to [[Hopkins High School]] in [[Minnetonka, Minnesota]]. As a senior, he averaged 24.1 points and 9.4 rebounds per game and led Hopkins to a Minnesota 4A state title over Lakeville North.{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Minnesota's Zeke Nnaji is third Arizona Wildcats recruit to win state title |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/minnesota-s-zeke-nnaji-is-third-arizona-wildcats-recruit-to/article_5df07b46-4df3-11e9-a50e-afe4036fbf32.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=November 26, 2019 |date=March 23, 2019}} Nnaji had 14 points and 12 rebounds in the championship game. He played for the Adidas-sponsored D1 Minnesota club alongside [[Matthew Hurt]]. Nnaji was invited to the Iverson Classic game. Nnaji was ranked 22nd in his class and a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] but was considered a four-star recruit by most other recruiting services.{{cite news |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=How Arizona's Zeke Nnaji slipped under the radar and became one of college basketball's early-season stars |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/how-arizona-s-zeke-nnaji-slipped-under-the-radar-and/article_a641c444-2694-5ff1-91e9-56966fbaa4c8.html |access-date=November 30, 2019 |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |date=November 20, 2019}} He committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].{{cite magazine |last=Geary |first=Molly |title=Arizona Moves to No. 1 in 2019 Recruiting Class Rankings With Commitment of Zeke Nnaji |url=https://www.si.com/college/2018/11/23/arizona-basketball-recruiting-sean-miller-zeke-nnaji |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=November 27, 2019 |date=November 23, 2018}} ==College career== On November 6, 2019, Nnaji made his college debut, scoring 20 points in 21 minutes to help Arizona defeat [[2019–20 Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball team|Northern Arizona]], 91–52.{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Freshman Zeke Nnaji's special debut calls to mind memories of D-Will, other Wildcats standouts |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/freshman-zeke-nnaji-s-special-debut-calls-to-mind-memories/article_c1067987-1a5f-5ce4-b825-bf5f5b3467d7.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=November 27, 2019 |date=November 7, 2019}} Five days later, he was named [[Pac-12 Conference]] Freshman of the Week.{{cite web |last=Scheer |first=Jason |title=Zeke Nnaji named Pac-12 Freshman of the Week |url=https://247sports.com/college/arizona/Article/Zeke-Nnaji-Pac-12-Freshman-of-the-Week-138449900/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=November 27, 2019 |date=November 11, 2019}} Nnaji won the same award in the following week, most notably posting 26 points and 11 rebounds in an 87–39 win over [[2019–20 San Jose State Spartans men's basketball team|San Jose State]].{{cite web |last=Pedersen |first=Brian J. |date=November 18, 2019 |title=Zeke Nnaji wins second straight Pac-12 Freshman of the Week award |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2019/11/18/20971319/zeke-nnaji-arizona-wildcats-pac12-freshman-award-weekly-basketball-2019 |access-date=November 27, 2019 |website=Arizona Desert Swarm|publisher=[[SB Nation]]}} He became the first Arizona player to score 20 points and collect 10 rebounds in his first three games since [[Brandon Ashley]] did so against [[Long Beach State Beach men's basketball|Long Beach State]] in the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 season]].{{cite news |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Freshman Zeke Nnaji could help bust zones thrown at Arizona Wildcats basketball |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2019/11/16/arizona-wildcats-basketball-zeke-nnaji-could-help-bust-zones-ua/4218300002/ |access-date=November 30, 2019 |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |date=November 16, 2019}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Nnaji was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 Freshman of the Year]].{{Cite web|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2020/03/08/2019-20-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards-announced|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326010600/https://pac-12.com/article/2020/03/08/2019-20-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards-announced|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 26, 2020|title=Pac-12 announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball annual major awards|date=March 9, 2020|website=pac-12.com|access-date=March 9, 2020}} Nnaji averaged 16.1 points per game on 57 percent shooting and grabbed 8.6 rebounds per game as a freshman. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Helin |first=Kurt |title=Arizona's Zeke Nnaji, DePaul's Paul Reed declare for NBA draft |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/03/29/arizonas-zeke-nnaji-depauls-paul-reed-declare-for-nba-draft/ |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 29, 2020|access-date=March 30, 2020}} ==Professional career== Nnaji was selected with the 22nd pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite news |last=Scheer |first=Jason |title=Zeke Nnaji drafted by the Denver Nuggets |url=https://247sports.com/college/arizona/Article/Zeke-Nnaji-drafted-by-the-Denver-Nuggets-154970085/ |access-date=November 18, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=November 18, 2020}} On December 1, 2020, Nnaji signed his rookie scale contract with the Nuggets.{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets sign Zeke Nnaji, R.J. Hampton to rookie contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-zeke-rj-20201201|date=December 1, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 1, 2020}} Nnaji became an [[NBA champion]] when the Nuggets defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in five games in the [[2023 NBA Finals]]. Nnaji signed a four-year, $32 million contract extension with the Nuggets on October 22, 2023.{{Cite web |title=Reports: Zeke Nnaji, Nuggets agree to 4-year, $32 million contract extension |url=https://www.nba.com/news/zeke-nnaji-nuggets-agree-to-4-year-32-million-contract-extension |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|champion=y}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2020}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2020–21 Denver Nuggets season|Denver]] | 42 || 1 || 9.5 || .481 || .407 || '''.800''' || 1.5 || .2 || .2 || .1 || 3.2 |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2021}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2021–22 Denver Nuggets season|Denver]] | 41 || 1 || '''17.0''' || .516 || '''.463''' || .631 || '''3.6''' || .4 || '''.4''' || .3 || '''6.6''' |- | style="text-align:left; His younger sister, Maya, played college basketball at Arizona for two years before quitting to pursue her education.{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Here's why Sean Miller says Zeke Nnaji, Arizona's bulked-up, piano-playing freshman, can do big things |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/here-s-why-sean-miller-says-zeke-nnaji-arizona-s/article_3e143706-c513-5337-9928-bc97150c9485.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=November 27, 2019 |date=September 14, 2019}} His uncle, Obiora Nnaji, played center at the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|University of Florida]] from 1997 to 1999.
